verses.pali: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to the Buddha,

verses.pali: “kati nu kho, bhante, loke dakkhiṇeyyā, kattha ca dānaṁ dātabban”ti?
verses.english: “How many in the world are worthy of a religious donation? And where should a gift be given?”
“Householder, there are two in the world who are worthy of a religious donation:

verses.pali: Ime kho, gahapati, dve loke dakkhiṇeyyā, ettha ca dānaṁ dātabban”ti.
verses.english: These two in the world are worthy of a religious donation, and that’s where you should give a gift.”
That is what the Buddha said.

verses.pali: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
verses.english: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“In this world, the trainee and the adept,
are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods.
This is the field for sponsors of sacrifice—
what’s given here is very fruitful.”
